Welcome Photography Digital Art

Art

I am an enthusiast photographer who mostly enjoys landscape and travel photography. You can see different categories of my works listed here in reverse chronological order, including both photography and digital art pieces. Additionally, I post some of the pieces on my instagram (@jwu_arts) account, so feel free to give it a follow if you are interested in seeing more or full-resolution versions of my works.

Photography

Landscapes and architecture photography let me explore how human history and nature intersect, framing stories through the textures of old cities and sweeping views of timeless scenes.

I started out with a Nikon D750 DSLR camera, paired with a 50-year-old 50mm manual-focus lens gifted by a friend – a setup that lasted me for years. Throughout my photographic journey, I've also used other digital cameras from Canon, Sony, Fujifilm, and others – but Nikon's pairing remained my favorite for its versatility, vintage-feel, anc accurate color representation.

Lately I've picked up film photography again after missing the dark room for ten years. Analog is such a physical medium that instantly allows me to recall the moment unlike anything in digital. Stay tuned for more experiments with film!

2025

Bend of 百里画廊 (Hundred-Mile Gallery)

Landscapes

  • A river carves its way through rolling meadows and pine forests, framed by the distant peaks of the Tianshan.
  • The gentle curve of the water captures the balance of stillness and motion that defines this storied valley.

果子沟大桥 (Guozigou Bridge)

Landscapes & Architecture

  • Against a backdrop of rugged green mountains and snow-capped peaks, cables rise like a modern monument in an ancient landscape.
  • The Guozigou Bridge is a marvel of engineering on the Lianhuo Expressway, which runs across the entirety of China. Countless shipping trucks soar through this bridge every day carrying goods from Kazakhstan to the Pacific.

Haystack with mountains of Xinjiang

  • A lone haystack stands in the foreground, while waves of hills, grassland, and jagged ridges recede into the misty distance.
  • I adore Xinjiang’s geographic richness, reflected in this layered composition — each horizon holds a new story in texture and light.

UChicago Campus

Landscapes & Architecture

  • The Ida Noyes Hall of the University of Chicago, with its classic architecture, red-and-white bricks, and duo-colored ivies.

Fog at Neuschwanstein Castle

Landscapes & Architecture

  • We visited the Neuschwanstein castles in a misty day – conditions quite typical for a central European summer. At one point the fog obscured our view completely. Just as we were heading down the mountains, the cloud cleared up, revealing the original inspiration behind Walt Disney’s castle.

Jungfrau, top of Europe

Landscapes & Nature

  • This photo was taken atop Jungfrau of the Swiss alps. The two houses in the foreground contrast with the expansive, rolling landscape of the back. It makes me imagine the details of its residents’ daily lives.

Venice Waterway

Landscapes & Architecture

  • The venetian city layout opens its way to many stunning, picturesque compositions. I especially appreciate the interminglement of water and traditional architectures.

Schloss Heidelberg

Landscapes & Architecture

  • This is the quintessential German experience – the misty clouds, green hills, dense trees, pointy castles, red roofs, white walls, and a winding road leading up to the Schloss Heidelberg.

Rome at Sunset

Landscapes & Architecture

  • Timeless elegance carved in the stones and shadows of Rome.
  • Photo shows the Ponte Sisto, arching gracefully across the Tiber. One of the most famous renaissance bridges, its worn stones carries centuries of footsteps, whispers, and sunsets over the Eternal City.
  • Landscapes and architecture photography let me explore how human history and nature intersect, framing stories through the textures of old cities and sweeping views of timeless scenes.

Sunset in Amsterdam

Landscapes & Architecture

  • Perhaps inspired by viewing “The Night Watch” at the National Museum of Netherland, I composed this photo with a similar motif of showing people of different walks of life gathered at the dusk of the city, gilded by the wanning light.

The Ismaning Town Hall

Landscapes & Architecture

  • I briefly stayed at the town of Ismaning, south of Garching bei München where I interned at the Max Planck Institute for summer of 2024. The town’s relaxed atmosphere made it perfect for me to wind down after an intense academic year.
  • This photo reflects this moment of tranquility: I had just arrived at a foreign country and taken the train to an unfamiliar town. The solemn ringings of the bell tower halted me on my journey to the hotel. Here, I reclaimed a slowness to life which I’ve lost for a long time.

Lamp Post and Blossoms

Stills

Salzburg

Landscapes & Architecture

  • With my friend visiting me in Munich, we took a trip to Salzburg, Austria. The city can be descrabed by a brush of green and blue, decorated with the traditional architectures of churches and castles.
  • Ascending to the top of the mountains, we are able to see down onto the vast flatlands, rolling into the Austrian alps down South. It was a view I won’t ever forget.

Sempre caro mi fu quest'ermo colle

Landscapes & Architecture

  • A small house in the middle of a field, in the Fermilab Batavia campus.
  • I had a lot of Italian influences from my time at Fermilab in the summer of 2023. This poem “L’infinito” came to mind when taking this photo.

Biking After Rain

Stills

  • Biking around the ring was one of my most fond memories at Fermilab. That day was going to be no different, but my passions were curbed by a sudden thunderstorm, which forced me into hiding.
  • I had just came out from a window sill, where I took shelter through the thunderstorm – the sun had done the same, it seemed, generously casting its rays onto the bike and the grass nearby.

Wilson Hall, Fermilab

Landscapes & Architecture

  • The Wilson Hall where I went to work everyday at Fermilab. It was such a towering figure in the middle of an essentially empty flatland, and thus it stands out especially among the architectures I’ve done science in.

Fireflies

Landscape

  • I saw fireflies for the first time at Fermilab, where it was dark and unpolluted enough for them to exist naturally. Those fleeting green dots captured my interests for quite a few days.
  • This photo was ontained from stacking together multiple 10.0s exposure shots. This was done to show the fireflies more clearly while not overblowing the background with a single exposure.

University of Pittsburgh

Landscapes & Architecture

  • This photo was accidentally obtained when adjusting the lighting on a not-so-ideal exposure. It captures the brooding prescence of the clouds. The architecture below is ignited by the rays that managed to escape the heavens.

Cherry Blossoms

Stills

  • The cherry blossoms bloom in spring, capturing fleeting moments of beauty at the University of Chicago campus.
  • I love stills with narrow field-of-view compositions, because they capture the quiet elegance of a single moment, preserving the beauty and fragility of life in perfect detail.

Flowers by the Regenstein Library

Stills

  • The white blossoms grow from bottom right to top left, rising against the beams of sunlight, which illuminates the edges of its young leaves. I believe this sufficiently showcases the beauty of nature and still lifes.

Happy Birthday!

Stills

  • A happy birthday message, taken of me drawing a light painting with my moon globe, and sent to someone special :).

Locks on Schenley Bridge

Stills

  • The Schenley Park, being one of my favorite localities in Pittsburgh, also hosts a bridge with locks on top. Many people come here to wish for a successful relationship, while I simply appreciated the intricate lock designs when I visited.

The Moon

Astrophotography

  • The moon, taken from my camera looking through the telescope atop the Ryerson Observatory at UChicago. The phase is wanning, and the photo shows in detail the transition between light and shadow on our planet’s only satellite.

Digital Art

Pixel art is easily my favorite style. I believe its minimalism is key for inspiring creativity and universality in the digital age. Similarly, vector art allows me to fuse my appreciation for technology into artistic expressions.
